reason_C: Rendered page (JAIR 70 p. 72, PDF p. 8): 'any non-trivial property ... of a Turing machine is undecidable. Non-trivial means some programs have that property and some don't.' Literal print is refuted (RiceLiteral.not_literalPrint: {Code.zero} is non-trivial and decidable); graded against the accepted repair (non-trivial extensional property). Program/Turing machine -> Nat.Partrec.Code with eval: print uses 'program' and 'Turing machine' interchangeably (Terminology box p. 69; 'some programs' in this very sentence) and fixes no model or encoding, so a standard program model is a value of what print leaves open (own, as both blind graders and the round-3 referees held). Property -> C : Set Code; undecidable (p. 69: no always-halting correct algorithm) -> not ComputablePred (fun code => code in C). If the tape automaton of the Terminology box were insisted on, the correspondence would be an argued step (equivalence of Turing and partial recursive computability with computable translations), not a scope change.
reason_A: Repaired print: C extensional and non-trivial. Lean rice_code_iff (Computability.lean:49-53): binder `extensional` renders the repair's condition (no effect); non-triviality is the negation of the right side of the iff (C = empty or C = univ <-> no member or no non-member, first-order logic). No other hypothesis. Same.
reason_B: Component (non-trivial extensional => undecidable): the -> direction of rice_code_iff, contraposed: same. Extra: the <- direction (the empty and the full property are decidable), a fact about print's own predicate (decidability of a property of programs) that print's component does not imply: stronger (B2, as E20). Both blind v6 graders call this Same by reverse certification (E40 pattern), deriving the <- direction from 'the constant procedure is computable'. That derivation uses no premise from print: it is an independent proof of the extra, which sec. 7.1 excludes as reverse evidence, and E40's extra (P 0) is an instance of print's own statement whereas this one is not. So B2/E20 decide as in v5.

reverse: Not certified for the whole statement: repaired print gives the -> direction (classical logic); the <- direction is proved independently of print (constant deciders), which is not a transfer through print's conclusion.
